annotationRationale: The divisor-count formula separates the objective into prime-exponent factors. Consecutive-factor ratios establish a strict maximum for every prime, yielding both a universal bound and the integer attaining it.
sourceMethod: Follows the official adjacent-exponent comparison method, using ratios to derive the same threshold inequalities and explaining why the individual strict maxima give the unique global maximum.

review.mathCheck: The consecutive-factor ratio exceeds 1 exactly when ((a+2)/(a+1))^3>p. The decreasing thresholds 8, 27/8, 64/27 and 125/64 give unique optimal exponents 3, 2, 1, 1 for primes 2, 3, 5, 7, and zero for every larger prime. Their simultaneous strict maxima give N=2520 and digit sum 9, choice E.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA Solution 25, pages 17–18: separate the prime-exponent factors and optimize them using consecutive ratios. The candidate additionally explains the divisor formula and global uniqueness.
review.annotationCheck: The argument handles exponent zero, every prime and all later exponents. It establishes an attainable universal maximum without calculus and is suitable for AMC 12.
